Abu Md Shah Newaz and others ----- Petitioners
Vs
Bangladesh and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment: The Court of appeal below take this statement and hold since this witness was a minor, may be at the age of 5/6 years, as such, no understandable capacity to understand what is permissive possession was grown in him and disbelieved the plaintiffs case and possession and also permissive possession on a wrong presumption. It is found that PW1 was 5/6 years old when permissive possession was given to defendant No. 3. It is not the case of defendant No. 3 that PW 1 was not living in the suit property such continuous living with his mother make him understand what is meant and understand by permissive possession. I will consider the case of permissive possession, the case of defendant No. 3 later on but at first the question as to whether plaintiff has been able to prove his possession and title by adverse possession is to be consider. From the aforesaid discussions of the Exhibits as well as depositions, the plaintiff at last could prove she is in possession of the suit land from 1958. The learned Advocate for the Government gave much emphasis on Exhibits 'ja', and 'jha' the proceedings of EP Case No. 52 of 1967-68 and EPL Case No. 119 of 1970-71, which are Exhibits relating to leasing of case land to different lessee. I find the first date appears therein is 24-3-67. I find Sufia Akter raised objections although. From the order dated 31-7-71 it appears the objection raised by Sufia Akter, the plaintiff, was rejected. It the body of the order the Superintendent Enemy Property (L&B) Comilla found all the owners of the above plots, namely Shantibhusan Deb, Tikendra Kumer Deb and Promod Deb, sons of Palash Chandra Deb and Khitesh Bhusan Deb, Narayan Deb and Shib Dulal Deb, who got the suit property through registered deed of gift dated 23.8.48, left the country and in absence of them, Begum Sufia Akhter manage the plots and manage to record the plots in her name. This fact goes to show the possession of plaintiff Learned Advocate for the Government while arguing the case, submits Government do not claim the land of Khitesh Chandra Deb as not enemy property. Although Exhibits 'ja' and lha' does not show Khitesh Chandra as the owner of the land. From Exhibit 'Jha', I find Sufia Akhter, the plaintiff although contested case by filing objection. Before 1968 there is no record on the part of the Government, excepting requisition proceeding, to prove Government ever tried to settle this land as Enemy Property or to that effect, in the alternative, as abandoned property. Requisition in the instant case is not for acquisition. Requisition means ownership of the property is retained by the owner. If it is the case of the Government that Government for acquisition of the property, requisitioned those lands from its owner Bhogaban Chandra Deb, then the Government case have at least a cripple structure. From Exhibit 17 series it appears Government de-requisitioned some non suited property in favour of Sufia Akhter at the appellate stage. The plaintiff filed applications (Exhibits 17 to 21) and Exhibit 17 speaks Government release the property of Requisition Case No. 291 of 1948 to Begum Sufia Akhter and it appears from Memorandum No. 2188 dated Comilla the 29-7-1954, wherein it has been stated, in the way of modification of the office order, "she is informed that the schedule shown in the above order has been replaced" and it is seen from this memorandum that possession of the house was made over to her on 7-7-54. Exhibit 18 is the receipt from Comilla Paurashava for payment of rent for the year of 1982-83. Exhibit 19 series and Exhibit 20 series shows plaintiffs paying taxes in respect of holding No. 471/433 and Exhibit 21 i.e. khatian No. 557 Stands in the name of Sufia Akhter. Although these are not directly relating to the suit plot No. 1925 but it goes to show remaining part of .the suit land requisitioned by the Government was released in favour of the plaintiff. Although the Government took up a point that its bharatia/ tenants are on the suit land. But if it is found the plaintiffs have acquired title against his vendor by adverse possession, the Government in no way could take over this property in either form, as enemy property or abandoned property. Since I have already found Exhibit 7 is a legal document and since I have found plaintiffs through different Exhibits as well as depositions and also from Exhibit Ja and Jha series prove her possession, I find plaintiff's case as to adverse possession in absence of any contrary evidence adduced by the defendants has been established because from the forgoing discussion it is seen the plaintiff's starting point of possession is from 1958 and suit having been filed on 15-9-1981, plaintiff possession is more than 12 years and these being no evidence, either oral or documentary to speak at any point of time plaintiff loses her possession, this possession in sufficient to confer her title by adverse possession against her vender.
